scope: Corollary 6.7 (Uniformity for the field wall) of the manuscript “The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale” (preprints/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 217 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e0e2e5e34169e701), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 65. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let the parent have data (3)–(5) and work on [s, 1], with s = o(a), at final strength e(q) = d2f(q/d) and lower wall 0 < rmin ≤ u∗/M(s). Suppose d = o(1) and d2 = o(ε). For 0 < ε ≤ T and 0 ≤ θ ≤ 1, put cL = 1 2 min(ε, T − ε), r0 = d2rmin 2ε , and take increasing 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1 on [0, s]. The bare algebraic coefficients are b0 = T − (ε + θcL)1u<s, h0 = θcLr0φ(u)1u<s. The profile conclusion of Proposition 6.6 holds uniformly along arbitrary sequences of these wall parameters, including θ → 0 and T − ε → 0.
